newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy advertising investment seen growing in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Italy advertising investment seen growing in 97/98.

text.p: Advertising investment in Italy is seen growing by 6.6 percent this year and will continue to grow in value terms over the next two years, the Italian advertising association UPA said.
UPA chairman Giulio Malgara, presenting a study on "The future of advertising", said the past years had been turbulent ones for the economy, consumption and the advertising sector.
"But 1996 marked the return to high rates of growth in the sector - the year of emerging from the tunnel of depression," UPA said in a statement.
The study showed that total advertising investments in 1996 were seen up 6.6 percent on 1995, against a rise of only 2.2 percent in 1994, at 21.56 trillion lire in value terms.
UAP said that forecasts for 1997 and 1998 showed a market in recovery, more contained in 1997 but stronger in 1998.

"Today the recovery in advertising investments point up the new trends which are changing the structure of the sector. The Italian market is more mature with respect to traditional consumer goods and at the same time part of the population is moving towards consumer goods with a higher service content," the UPA statement said.

Total advertising investment in 1997 was forecast growing an annual 4.9 percent rising to 5.7 percent in 1998, but in value terms investment was seen at 22.62 trillion lire and 23.91 trillion lire respectively.

By sectors, investment in advertising in the printed press was seen slipping from 6.9 percent this year to 4.5 percent in 1998 and that in television advertising falling from 7.0 percent this year to 5.9 percent in 1998.

But investment in direct response was seen rising from 6.5 percent this year to 7.0 percent in 1998, that in public relations rising from 5.9 percent to 6.5 percent, and in sponsorship increasing from 4.7 percent to 5.0 percent.
